To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the structural proteins of alphaviruses interact with nonstructural proteins and sequence elements within the genome, that these interactions contribute to efficient RNA replication, that these interactions appear to be suboptimal in chimeras between two alphavirus species, and that this may limit the establishment of naturally occurring chimeras between distinct alphaviruses.

we have constructed two chimeric viruses, one containing Ross River virus nonstructural proteins in a Sindbis virus structural protein background and the other containing Sindbis virus structural proteins in a Ross River virus non-structural protein background, and that the chimeras are viable but have reduced replication capacities in comparison with the parents.

the structural and non-structural regions of the alphaviruses are functionally interdependent, and that the non-structural/structural chimera viruses that might be formed by natural recombination events are likely to be viable but that their growth will be limited.
